entities.name: Autun Cathedral
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
Autun Cathedral (Cathédrale Saint-Lazare d'Autun) in Burgundy, France, built 1120-1146 CE and expanded later, is one of the supreme monuments of Romanesque sculpture — most notably for the tympanum over the central west portal depicting the Last Judgment, carved c. 1130-1145 CE and signed by the sculptor 'Gislebertus hoc fecit' (Gislebertus made this) — making it the rare case of a signed medieval sculptural masterpiece. The Gislebertus tympanum is widely considered the greatest Romanesque sculptural program north of the Alps.

Gislebertus's Last Judgment — depicting a serene but awesome Christ in majesty, with souls being weighed in the balance, the blessed rising to heaven in orderly columns, and the damned seized by enormous demonic hands in extraordinary expressions of terror — represents the high point of Romanesque sculpture's dramatic, expressive power. The individual capitals in the nave (some now in the Autun Rolin Museum to protect them) include the Flight into Egypt, the Three Magi asleep, and the Temptation of Eve — the latter (now in the Metropolitan Museum, New York) being one of the most sensuously expressive medieval sculptures in existence.

Autun was founded by Augustus as the Roman city of Augustodunum, capital of the Aedui tribe, and its Roman heritage (including two surviving Roman gates — Porte d'Arroux and Porte Saint-André) makes it one of France's richest sites for Roman-medieval continuity. The cathedral's dedication to St. Lazarus (whose relics were brought from Marseille) made it a significant pilgrimage destination. The tympanum survived the Revolution only because it was plastered over in 1766 and not discovered until 1837.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Autun Cathedral — containing Gislebertus's signed Last Judgment tympanum (the supreme Romanesque sculpture north of the Alps), the Temptation of Eve (among history's most beautiful medieval sculptures), and sitting on a Roman imperial city — is one of the most artistically and historically significant medieval monuments in Europe.
